newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to deal better with lone foreign children.
newsitem.headline: EU to deal better with lone foreign children.

text.p: Children and young people who run away or are smuggled into the European Union will be entitled to better treatment by the authorities under an accord reached by the bloc's justice ministers on Monday.
Under the agreement, people aged under 18 from a third country who turn up in the EU unaccompanied by an adult will be entitled to special treatment.
Although the accord is not legally binding, EU governments have agreed to abide by it.
Authorities will have to establish the minor's identity quickly, locate his or her family, provide legal representation, give priority to their request for asylum and provide medical care.
They can only be returned home once it has been established that they will be looked after once they return.
EU Justice Commissioner Anita Gradin told reporters that one result of the agreement would be that the young people would have to be dealt with by specialised workers and dealt with in a "good way".
